'''Dyson Daniels''' (born 17 March 2003) is an Australian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]].

==Early life and career==
Daniels was born in [[Bendigo]], [[Australia]] and started playing basketball at age seven.<ref name=fiba>{{cite web |title=Boomers' phenom will have you shouting "Damn, Daniels!" |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/asiacup/2021/qualifiers/news/boomer-s-phenom-will-have-you-shouting-damn-daniels |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=21 February 2021}}</ref> He signed with the [[Bendigo Braves]], his father's former team, of the [[NBL1]] for the [[2019 NBL1 season|2019 season]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Iles |first1=Kieran |title=Dyson Daniels keen to forge his own identity with Bendigo Braves |url=https://www.bendigoadvertiser.com.au/story/5925221/dyson-daniels-keen-to-forge-his-own-identity-with-bendigo-braves/ |website=[[Bendigo Advertiser]] |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=26 February 2019}}</ref> Later that year, Daniels joined the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] Global Academy, a training center at the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] in [[Canberra]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Garlepp |first1=Josh |title=Dyson Daniels is the NBA Global Academy’s latest star, with an admirable goal in mind |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/dyson-daniels-is-the-nba-global-academys-newest-star-with-an-admirable-goal-in-mind/news-story/9a1338f014f554819afa80af41cc01f0 |website=[[Fox Sports (Australia)|Fox Sports]] |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=1 March 2020}}</ref> He helped Victoria win a silver medal at the 2021 Australian Under-20 Championships.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bourke |first1=Adam |title=Daniels dominates for Victoria at national championships |url=https://www.bendigoadvertiser.com.au/story/7243777/daniels-dominates-for-victoria-at-national-championships/ |website=[[Bendigo Advertiser]] |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=8 May 2021}}</ref> Along with basketball, Daniels was a talented [[Australian rules football]]er in his younger years and represented his home state of [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] at several national football championships<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tuckerman |first1=Raelee |title=Dyson sports Big V |url=https://www.bendigoadvertiser.com.au/story/3122974/dyson-sports-big-v/ |website=[[Bendigo Advertiser]] |access-date=13 January 2022 |date=3 June 2015}}</ref> before giving up the sport to focus solely on basketball.

==Professional career==
On 21 June 2021, Daniels signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]], a developmental team affiliated with the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=International Standout Dyson Daniels Signs With NBA G League Ignite |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/international-standout-dyson-daniels-signs-with-nba-g-league-ignite/ |publisher=[[NBA G League]] |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=21 June 2021}}</ref> He turned down offers from several college programs and the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] Next Stars program.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=NBA's G League Ignite sign first highly touted international prospect in Australia's Dyson Daniels |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31674738/nba-g-league-ignite-signs-first-highly-touted-international-prospect-australia-dyson-daniels |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=20 June 2021}}</ref>

On 16 April 2022, Daniels declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Australian guard Dyson Daniels, the No. 10 prospect in the ESPN 100, to enter the 2022 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33751931/australian-guard-dyson-daniels-no-10-prospect-espn-100-enter-2022-nba-draft |access-date=April 16, 2022 |website=ESPN}}</ref> Daniels reportedly grew from 6’6” to 6’8” while preparing for the draft .<ref name=":0" />

==National team career==
Daniels represented Australia at the 2018 [[FIBA Oceania]] Under-15 Championship in [[Papua New Guinea]]. He averaged 8.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game, helping his team win the gold medal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dyson Daniels (AUS)'s profile – FIBA U15 Oceania Championship 2018 |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/oceania/u15/2018/player/Dyson-Daniels |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref> On 20 February 2021, Daniels made his debut for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian senior national team]] at [[2021 FIBA Asia Cup qualification|FIBA Asia Cup qualification]].<ref name=ward>{{cite web |last1=Ward |first1=Roy |title=‘He’s kind of unique, a throwback’: Dyson Daniels follows in Ben Simmons’ footsteps in making Boomers debut |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/he-s-kind-of-unique-a-throwback-dyson-daniels-follows-in-ben-simmons-footsteps-in-making-boomers-debut-20210219-p573y2.html |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=19 February 2021}}</ref> He recorded 23 points, six steals and four assists in an 81–52 win over [[New Zealand men's national basketball team|New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kidane |first1=Benyam |title=Dyson Daniels leads young Aussie Boomers to impressive win over New Zealand in FIBA Asia Cup qualifier |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/nba/news/dyson-daniels-leads-young-australian-boomers-win-over-new-zealand-fiba-asia-cup-qualifier/17xvq05d39hm81n86tpzy70514 |website=[[Sporting News]] |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=20 February 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Daniels' father, Ricky, is from the United States and played [[college basketball]] at [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] before embarking on a professional career.<ref name=fiba/> He was a two-time [[South East Australian Basketball League]] MVP with the [[Bendigo Braves]], and his number was retired by the team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dyson Daniels to emulate his father, Ricky, and play for Braves |url=https://www.bendigoadvertiser.com.au/story/5920207/like-father-like-son-dyson-daniels-to-play-for-braves-senior-team/ |website=[[Bendigo Advertiser]] |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=22 February 2019}}</ref> Daniels' older brother, Kai, plays college basketball at [[Regis Rangers|Regis University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dyson Daniels |url=https://www.prospectiveinsight.com/post/dyson-daniels |website=Pro Insight |access-date=21 June 2021 |date=30 October 2020}}</ref>
